parsed.explanation: No traveller-facing exposure is documented: same-sex conduct decriminalised since 1996 with offences treated identically, no gender-expression offence, no reported police targeting of trans people, no facility ban, no custody rule, no recorded anti-trans violence or border refusals. The heavy documented negatives are resident-facing gaps (no gender-marker change, eight rejected requests, no marriage/civil union, DV-law exclusion), which rule 1 bars me from charging to a visitor whose documents come from home. Remaining drags are climate: an explicitly values-based refusal to accommodate gender identity, 'lack of social consensus', invisible queer life, a pathologising education official and a 'gay demon' headline — friction and disapproval, not state threat-framing. Open questions (border practice, facilities, custody, whether sectoral protections cover gender identity) are light, and thin data means silence earns no credit. Sits above the 0.55 tier (documented recurring visitor harms) and below 0.65 (documented working remedies or acceptance).
